ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart friend who can solve complex math problems, but they can't explain how they do it. That's kinda like what's happening with these big neural networks. They're so complex that even the people who created them, like the "kun" who made ChatGPT, don't fully understand how they work, "genki desu ka?" (are you okay?). It's like trying to describe a beautiful painting to someone who's never seen it, "kirei desu" (it's beautiful).

These neural networks are made up of many layers of interconnected nodes, or "neuron" (neuron), that process information in a way that's not always easy to understand, "honto ni kowai" (it's really scary). The creators can tweak and adjust the network to make it better, but they can't always see the underlying "mechanism" (mechanism), "kakete iru" (it's hidden).

It's like trying to describe a dream to someone who's never had one, "yume o tsukamu" (to capture a dream). The creators can make the network do cool things, like generate art or answer questions, but they can't always explain why it's working, "nani ga koto desu ka?" (what's going on?). So, they just keep tweaking and adjusting, hoping to get better results, "kakete iru" (it's hidden).
